subject: Handling Outliers in Hierarchical Model with Two Parameters for which I estimate the Correlation

messages.author: e1af1b5e367974aa
messages.subject: Handling Outliers in Hierarchical Model with Two Parameters for which I estimate the Correlation
parts:
Hello all,

I have a hierarchical model for which the primary outcome is the relationship between the effect of attention on the following two parameters: Rho and PSS. (The code for .stan model can be found at https://github.com/ghislaindentremont/EndogenousVisualPriorEntry-BayesianHierarchicalModel/blob/master/Baseball/toj_color.stan.) 

My model estimates the correlation between these effects (see violin plot of correlation parameter (r), attached). However, I was also interested at looking at the bivariate plot to get a better sense of the relationship of these effects. Therefore, I computed the participant-wise estimates of these effects by adding the estimate (median) of the mean of the effect to the product of the estimate (median) of the SD of the effect and the estimate (median) of the participant-wise deviation of the effect. If you look at the related scatterplot (attached), you'll see that there is at least one outlying point (bottom left) that appears to have a lot of leverage. Although I believe my model is fairly robust to such outliers, I believe that that one point may be having too much leverage on the estimate of the correlation parameter. However, I don't think I want to exclude that participant from the analysis all together...

Is there a way I can deal with this/these outlier(s) within the model to get what might be a better estimate of the correlation coefficient? 

You will notice that in the linked code that I use bivariate normals as priors. I am currently running a full analysis (8 chains, 20,000 iterations each) with student_ts with nu = 3 as priors to see how that may effect the model's robustness to outliers. Although, I am not under the impression that it will change much given that the outlying values were within one SD of the normal priors. 

If anything is unclear, let me know. 

Looking forward to your responses,

Ghislain d'Entremont, BSc., Experimental Psychology Researcher

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Handling Outliers in Hierarchical Model with Two Parameters for which I estimate the Correlation
parts:
Not my area of expertise, but given that nobody else
has responded, I'll take a stab. The only way I know how
to do this without any extra information is to use a fatter-tailed
distribution for the error terms, and it looks like that's what
you're doing with the Student-t. An alternative would be to
try to bring in some other predictors, like time series or
individual effects to model the variation directly rather than
rolling it all into the error term of a regression.

In general, correlations are hard to estimate---you'll typically
see wide posteriors. So you might want to scatterplot draws
from the posterior rather than summarizing with a median.

You could also fit without that point and see what the effect is.

- Bob
